summary: Stanley Weinstein specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa, Tokyo, and Harvard universities under Kodo Sawaki, Gyokusen Hosaka, and Masatoshi Nagatomi. He taught at Komazawa, SOAS (~1962–1968), and Yale University from 1968.

Stanley Wolpert was a scholar of Indology and history. He earned his B.A. from the City College of New York (~1949–1953) and his M.A. from the University of Pennsylvania (~1953–1955), subsequently serving at UCLA as assistant professor (1959), associate professor (1963), and department chair (1967).
Stefan Anacker worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Alex Wayman from ~1965 to 1970.

Stefan Baums specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at the University of Washington (2002–2009) and held research positions at the Göttingen Academy (2009–2011), University of Munich (~2011), and Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (from ~2012).

Stefan Larsson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Stockholm University under Per-Arne Berglie and Erik af Edholm, also studying under David Germano, and was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley (attested 2012).

Stefan M. Maul is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Free University of Berlin, later holding posts as Ordinarius at Heidelberg University (1995) and research unit head at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2004).

Stefania Travagnin works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor and centre director at the University of Groningen (~2013–2020) before joining SOAS University of London in ~2020.

Stefano Zacchetti was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his BA and PhD at Ca' Foscari University under Alfredo Cadonna and others. He held posts at Soka University (2001–2005) and Oxford University (2012–2020).

Steffen Döll works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his M.A. and doctorate at the University of Munich, where he was an assistant (2008–2015), and became Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism at the University of Hamburg in 2015.

Stella Kramrisch was an Indologist and art historian who earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna under Max Dvořák and Josef Strzygowski. She held faculty positions at Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, the University of Pennsylvania (1950–1993), and NYU (1964–1982).

Sten Konow was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Oslo and Halle-Wittenberg under Sophus Bugge and Richard Pischel, holding professorships at the University of Oslo and the University of Hamburg (1914–1919).
Stephan Beyer specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1977).
Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephanie Kaza specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Oberlin, Stanford, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry under Thích Nhất Hạnh and Joanna Macy, later serving as professor at the University of Vermont (1991–2015).
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her doctoral studies under Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison specializes in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed doctoral work at Yale under Stanley Insler and Warren Crawford Cowgill and was appointed professor at UCLA in ~2002.
Stephen A. Murphy is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his MA and doctoral studies under Elizabeth H. Moore at SOAS University of London.

Stephen Addiss specialized in Japanology and art history. He earned degrees from Harvard and the University of Michigan, subsequently serving as professor of art history at the University of Kansas (1977–1992) and Tucker-Boatwright Professor at the University of Richmond (1992–2013).

Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied with Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim. He was a translator at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg (1979), director of Sharpham College (~1992–2000), and core faculty at Bodhi College (~2015).

Stephen C. Berkwitz works in Buddhist and religious studies. He held a Fulbright fellowship at the University of Kelaniya (1995–1997) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Missouri State University (attested 2013).
